title: ArborMem: Navigating Interaction States with Memory Forests
abstract: arXiv:2608.17534v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models increasingly serve as persistent conversational assistants, requiring memory that preserves relevant experience and maintains continuity across interactions. Existing methods improve access to conversational history through long-context processing, selective retrieval, and structured memory organization. However, most systems treat memory access as retrieving relevant past information without first determining which prior interaction state the current turn resumes. This limitation becomes particularly important when conversations interleave multiple tasks, people, and plans that may be interrupted and later revisited. We introduce ArborMem, an online memory framework that represents a long-running conversation as a navigable forest of interaction states. translated_title: ArborMem：以记忆森林导航交互状态
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型日益成为持久的对话助手，需要记忆来保留相关经验并维持跨交互的连续性。现有方法通过长上下文处理、选择性检索和结构化记忆组织来改善对对话历史的访问。然而，大多数系统将记忆访问视为检索相关的过去信息，而没有首先确定当前轮次恢复的是哪个先前的交互状态。当对话交织多个任务、人物和计划，且这些内容可能被中断后重新访问时，这一局限性变得尤为重要。我们引入了ArborMem，一种在线记忆框架，将长时间运行的对话表示为可导航的交互状态森林。每个分支保留局部连贯的轨迹，而森林则维护可能稍后恢复的多个轨迹。对于每个新输入，ArborMem定位……
tldr: ArborMem提出了一种将长时间对话建模为可导航交互状态森林的在线记忆框架，通过先定位当前轮次恢复的先前状态，再导航记忆，解决了多任务交织对话中的记忆访问问题。
en_tdlr: ArborMem introduces an online memory framework that models long-running conversations as a navigable forest of interaction states, addressing memory access by first localizing the prior state resumed by the current turn, thus improving multi-task interleaved dialogue handling.
